newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Triple murderer loses bid to stay in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Triple murderer loses bid to stay in Australia.

text.p: Triple murderer Archie "Mad Dog" McCafferty failed in a last-ditch bid to remain in Australia on Wednesday and faces imminent deportation to Britain.
McCafferty, who was granted parole last week after 23 years in jail, lost an appeal to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal against a deportation order by the Australian government.
"He will be deported as soon as arrangements can be made," an immigration department spokeswoman told Reuters.
She declined to give any date for his return, which has sparked some controversy in Britain, although the British goverment has said it accepts the decision.
Glasgow-born McCafferty, 49, was sentenced to life in jail in 1974 as the leader of a gang which killed three men in Sydney in five days after his baby son suffocated while breastfeeding.
McCafferty, who came to Australia with his family at the age of 10 but never became an Australian citizen, said he had suffered a delusion telling him to kill seven people.
Australian media nicknamed McCafferty "Mad Dog" because of his killings.
The New South Wales Parole Board last week said McCafferty had been seen as a model prisoner since 1988 and ordered his release by May 3.
